justifications.1: Names expense claim review against receipts and the supplied policy.
justifications.2: Output template with per-item verdict, cited basis, totals, questions and a sentence-capped summary.
justifications.3: States the review ends when every item has a verdict, totals reconcile and questions exist, and that the approver decides.
justifications.4: Explicit cases for missing policy, missing receipt (by clause type) and receipt mismatches.
justifications.5: Authority per input, policy-only, and pre-approval notes treated as claims to verify.
justifications.6: Thorough but about 1,200 words with the missing-input rules ahead of the steps, which crowds the common path.

justifications.1: Clearly scoped to expense claim review against a supplied policy.
justifications.2: Table, totals and per-line evidence trail with questions and summary defined.
justifications.3: Per-step done-when conditions but no statement that nothing further is expected.
justifications.4: Missing claim form or policy halts with a request; missing receipts and mismatches become needs-information lines.
justifications.5: Policy-only rulebook stated, but nothing on notes or approvals inside the files.
justifications.6: Compact; receipt checks sit after the main steps.

justifications.1: Triggers on claim form, receipts and policy to check or approve.
justifications.2: Verdict rules, basis format, total arithmetic and summary content are all specified.
justifications.3: Step done-whens only; no explicit end state.
justifications.4: Missing inputs prompt a request; missing or mismatched receipts have explicit handling.
justifications.5: Policy-only and unmatched receipts not reimbursed, but no handling of approvals or instructions in the files.
justifications.6: Short and well proportioned.

justifications.1: Names reviewing, checking or auditing an expense claim against policy.
justifications.2: Verdict definitions, evidence line, total with reductions, questions and summary are defined.
justifications.3: Ends with a check against the inventory but never says no further work is expected.
justifications.4: Asks for missing policy or form; missing, illegible and conflicting receipts handled via verdict rules.
justifications.5: Policy as whole rulebook, but no rule on treating pre-approval notes or embedded instructions as non-authoritative.
justifications.6: Proportionate, with a single closing check.

justifications.1: Triggers on claim form, receipts and policy to check or approve.
